title: Algebra I
description: Build from equations and functions to quadratics, exponentials, and data.

lessons.title: Units and precision
lessons.reading: A quantity needs both a number and a unit. Dimensional analysis multiplies by conversion factors equal to one. A model should use a sensible domain: counts are whole numbers, while measurements may be continuous.
lessons.worked: A 90-minute trip lasts 90/60 = 1.5 hours. At 40 miles per hour, distance is 60 miles.

application.prompt: A runner travels 12 miles in 2 hours. What is the average speed?
application.explanation: Divide distance by time, keeping miles in the numerator and hours in the denominator.

vocab.definition: A measurable property expressed with a number and unit.
The permitted inputs of a relation or function.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Divide distance by time, keeping miles in the numerator and hours in the denominator.

lessons.title: Equivalent expressions
lessons.reading: Equivalent expressions have the same value for every allowed input. Distribute multiplication over every term and combine only like terms. A coefficient multiplies a variable expression; an exponent tells a power.

application.prompt: Which expression equals 2(x − 3) + 4x?
application.explanation: Distribution gives 2x − 6 + 4x. Combine the x-terms, keeping the constant −6.

vocab.definition: A numerical factor multiplying a variable term.
Expressions with equal values for every permitted input.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Distribution gives 2x − 6 + 4x. Combine the x-terms, keeping the constant −6.

lessons.title: Real numbers and radicals
lessons.reading: Rational numbers are ratios of integers. Irrational numbers cannot be written that way. Simplify square roots using perfect-square factors. The principal square root is nonnegative, so √(x²) = absolute value of x.
lessons.worked: √72 = √(36 × 2) = 6√2, an exact value.

application.prompt: Which is √50 in simplest radical form?
application.explanation: Factor 50 as 25 × 2 and take the square root of the perfect-square factor.

vocab.definition: A number expressible as a ratio of integers with nonzero denominator.
The expression inside a radical symbol.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Factor 50 as 25 × 2 and take the square root of the perfect-square factor.

lessons.title: Equations as balanced relationships
lessons.reading: Solve an equation by applying the same reversible operation to both sides. Simplify first, collect variable terms, and isolate the variable. An equation can have one solution, no solution, or all real numbers as solutions.
lessons.worked: 3x − 5 = 16 becomes 3x = 21, so x = 7.

application.prompt: Solve 4x + 3 = 19.
application.explanation: Subtract 3 from both sides, then divide by 4. Substitute 4 to check the original equation.

vocab.definition: A value that makes an equation or inequality true.
An equation true for every allowed value.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Subtract 3 from both sides, then divide by 4. Substitute 4 to check the original equation.

lessons.title: Literal equations
lessons.reading: A formula relates several quantities. Isolate the requested variable using inverse operations, treating other symbols as constants. State restrictions when you divide by a variable expression.
lessons.worked: From A = bh/2, multiply by 2 and divide by nonzero b: h = 2A/b.

application.prompt: Rearrange d = rt for t, when r ≠ 0.
application.explanation: Dividing both sides by r isolates the time variable.

vocab.definition: An equation containing multiple variables.
Operations that reverse one another.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Dividing both sides by r isolates the time variable.

lessons.title: Inequalities and intervals
lessons.reading: Inequalities describe ranges of values. Multiplying or dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality sign. A strict inequality excludes the endpoint. A compound inequality combines conditions with and or or.
lessons.worked: −2x < 8 becomes x > −4. The sign reverses because we divide by −2.

application.prompt: Solve −3x ≥ 12.
application.explanation: Division by a negative number reverses the ordering. Check with x = −5, which gives 15 ≥ 12.

vocab.definition: A statement comparing quantities using an order relation.
Two or more inequalities joined by and or or.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Division by a negative number reverses the ordering. Check with x = −5, which gives 15 ≥ 12.

lessons.title: Slope and intercepts
lessons.reading: A linear function changes at a constant rate. In y = mx + b, m is slope and b is the y-intercept. Slope is change in output divided by change in input. Vertical lines have undefined slope and are not y-functions.
lessons.worked: Through (1,3) and (3,7), slope is (7 − 3)/(3 − 1) = 2.

application.prompt: A line has slope 3 and passes through (0,−2). Its equation is…
application.explanation: The point with x = 0 supplies the y-intercept, while the stated slope is the coefficient of x.

vocab.definition: The ratio of vertical change to horizontal change.
Where a graph meets the y-axis.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: The point with x = 0 supplies the y-intercept, while the stated slope is the coefficient of x.

lessons.title: Write and compare models
lessons.reading: Translate an initial amount into an intercept and a per-unit change into a slope. Compare two linear plans by finding where their outputs match. Interpret the intersection using the original units.
lessons.worked: Plan A costs 10 + 2x; Plan B costs 4 + 3x. They cost the same at x = 6.

application.prompt: A taxi charges $5 plus $2 per mile. What is the cost for 4 miles?
application.explanation: The fixed charge is added once: 5 + 2(4) = 13.

vocab.definition: A model with a constant rate of change.
Output change per unit of input change.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: The fixed charge is added once: 5 + 2(4) = 13.

lessons.title: Systems and feasible regions
lessons.reading: A solution to a system satisfies every equation or inequality. Use substitution, elimination, or intersection. A system of inequalities has a feasible region rather than just a point; dashed boundaries exclude equality.
lessons.worked: y = x + 1 and x + y = 7 give x = 3 and y = 4.

application.prompt: Which ordered pair solves y = 2x and x + y = 9?
application.explanation: Substitute y = 2x: 3x = 9, giving x = 3 and y = 6. Both equations must hold.

vocab.definition: A collection of equations or inequalities considered simultaneously.
The set satisfying all constraints in a system.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Substitute y = 2x: 3x = 9, giving x = 3 and y = 6. Both equations must hold.

lessons.title: Functions and notation
lessons.reading: A function assigns exactly one output to each input in its domain. Function notation names an output, not multiplication. Tables and graphs can show functions; the vertical-line test checks whether a graph assigns more than one y-value to an x-value.
lessons.worked: If f(x) = x² − 1, then f(3) = 9 − 1 = 8.

application.prompt: For f(x) = 2x + 5, f(−2) equals…
application.explanation: Replace every x with −2 and follow the order of operations: −4 + 5 = 1.

vocab.definition: A relation assigning one output to each permitted input.
The set of outputs of a relation or function.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Replace every x with −2 and follow the order of operations: −4 + 5 = 1.

lessons.title: Arithmetic and geometric sequences
lessons.reading: A sequence is a function on ordered integer inputs. Arithmetic sequences add a common difference; geometric sequences multiply by a common ratio. An explicit rule finds a term directly, while a recursive rule uses earlier terms.
lessons.worked: The sequence 4, 7, 10 has a common difference of 3 and rule a(n) = 4 + 3(n − 1).

application.prompt: Which is the next term of 3, 6, 12, 24?
application.explanation: Each term is twice the preceding term, so multiply 24 by 2.

vocab.definition: A sequence with a constant difference.
A sequence with a constant ratio.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Each term is twice the preceding term, so multiply 24 by 2.

lessons.title: Read and transform graphs
lessons.reading: Interpret intercepts, increasing intervals, maxima, minima, and end behavior in context. Adding k outside f shifts a graph vertically by k. Replacing x by x − h shifts it right by h. A graph's useful domain may be restricted.
lessons.worked: g(x) = f(x) + 3 raises each output by 3 without changing the input.

application.prompt: How does g(x) = f(x) − 4 change the graph?
application.explanation: Subtracting outside the function changes every output by −4.

vocab.definition: A rule changing the position or shape of a graph.
A greatest function value on a specified domain.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Subtracting outside the function changes every output by −4.

lessons.title: Absolute value and piecewise rules
lessons.reading: Absolute value measures distance from zero. A piecewise function uses different rules on specified input intervals. Check interval endpoints carefully; the function must assign one output per input. Step and absolute-value graphs model different types of change.
lessons.worked: A fee is $4 for x ≤ 2 and $4 + 2(x − 2) for x > 2; the correct rule depends on x.

application.prompt: What is absolute value of −7?
application.explanation: Distance from zero is nonnegative, so the absolute value of −7 is 7.

vocab.definition: Distance from zero on the number line.
A function defined by different rules on specified parts of its domain.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Distance from zero is nonnegative, so the absolute value of −7 is 7.

lessons.title: Polynomial structure
lessons.reading: A polynomial is a sum of terms with nonnegative integer exponents on its variables. Degree is the greatest term degree after simplification. Add like terms and multiply using distribution. Structure often reveals a useful factorization.

application.prompt: Expand (x + 4)(x − 1).
application.explanation: Multiply all pairs: x² − x + 4x − 4, then combine the x-terms.

vocab.definition: A finite sum of terms with nonnegative integer variable exponents.
The greatest term degree of a nonzero polynomial.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Multiply all pairs: x² − x + 4x − 4, then combine the x-terms.

lessons.title: Factor common factors and trinomials
lessons.reading: Factoring rewrites a sum as a product. Remove a greatest common factor first. For x² + bx + c, look for numbers whose sum is b and product is c. A difference of squares has form a² − b².

application.prompt: Factor x² + 5x + 6.
application.explanation: The needed pair adds to 5 and multiplies to 6: 2 and 3.

vocab.definition: An expression multiplied with another to form a product.
The greatest factor shared by all terms.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: The needed pair adds to 5 and multiplies to 6: 2 and 3.

lessons.title: Zeros and products
lessons.reading: A zero of a function is an input with output zero. The zero-product property applies when a product equals zero. Set each variable factor equal to zero. Dividing by a variable can accidentally remove a valid zero solution.
lessons.worked: x(x − 5) = 0 has zeros 0 and 5.

application.prompt: The zeros of (x − 2)(x + 4) are…
application.explanation: A product is zero when either factor is zero. Solve x − 2 = 0 and x + 4 = 0.

vocab.definition: An input at which a function equals zero.
If a product is zero, at least one factor is zero.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: A product is zero when either factor is zero. Solve x − 2 = 0 and x + 4 = 0.

lessons.title: Exponent rules and structure
lessons.reading: For common bases, multiplying powers adds exponents and dividing subtracts them when denominators are nonzero. Raising a power to a power multiplies exponents. Zero and negative exponents describe relationships preserving these rules, not new arithmetic exceptions.
lessons.worked: For x ≠ 0, x⁵/x² = x³ and x⁻² = 1/x².

application.prompt: Simplify x³ · x⁴.
application.explanation: There are seven total factors of x in the product, so the exponent is 3 + 4.

vocab.definition: An exponent indicating a reciprocal power.
An expression whose exponents multiply when simplified.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: There are seven total factors of x in the product, so the exponent is 3 + 4.

lessons.title: Parabolas and vertex form
lessons.reading: A quadratic function has degree two and graphs as a parabola. In y = a(x − h)² + k, the vertex is (h,k) and the symmetry axis is x = h. The sign of a determines whether the vertex is a minimum or maximum.
lessons.worked: y = (x − 2)² − 3 has vertex (2,−3) and a minimum of −3.

application.prompt: What is the vertex of y = (x + 1)² + 4?
application.explanation: Rewrite x + 1 as x − (−1). Vertex form identifies h = −1 and k = 4.

vocab.definition: The turning point of a parabola.
A line across which a figure reflects onto itself.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Rewrite x + 1 as x − (−1). Vertex form identifies h = −1 and k = 4.

lessons.title: Solve quadratics in different ways
lessons.reading: Factoring, square roots, completing the square, and the quadratic formula solve quadratic equations. First write standard form when using coefficients. Real solutions correspond to x-intercepts. A negative discriminant means no real roots.
lessons.worked: x² − 6x + 5 = 0 factors into (x − 1)(x − 5) = 0.

application.prompt: Solve x² = 49 over the real numbers.
application.explanation: Both 7 and −7 square to 49. The equation has two solutions even though √49 is 7.

vocab.definition: The expression b² − 4ac classifying quadratic roots.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Both 7 and −7 square to 49. The equation has two solutions even though √49 is 7.

lessons.title: Quadratic models and intersections
lessons.reading: Use quadratics for relationships involving squared quantities, area, or constant acceleration. An intersection with a line satisfies both rules. Reject solutions outside a model's meaningful domain, but explain why rather than removing negatives automatically.
lessons.worked: For y = x² and y = x + 2, x² − x − 2 = 0 gives intersections (−1,1) and (2,4).

application.prompt: A rectangle has sides x and x + 2 and area 24. Its positive width is…
application.explanation: x(x + 2) = 24 factors into (x + 6)(x − 4) = 0. Width must be positive, so choose 4.

vocab.definition: A point belonging to each of two graphs.
A restriction on allowed values.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: x(x + 2) = 24 factors into (x + 6)(x − 4) = 0. Width must be positive, so choose 4.

lessons.title: Growth and decay factors
lessons.reading: Exponential models multiply by the same factor over equal input intervals. In y = a(b)^t, a is the initial amount and b the growth factor. A rate r gives factor 1 + r for growth or 1 − r for decay.
lessons.worked: A value growing 5% yearly has factor 1.05, not 5.

application.prompt: A $200 item loses 10% yearly. Its value after one year is…
application.explanation: Ten percent of 200 is 20. Subtract it, or multiply 200 by 0.90.

vocab.definition: A function with the variable in an exponent and constant positive base.
The fraction retained after each equal time interval.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Ten percent of 200 is 20. Subtract it, or multiply 200 by 0.90.

lessons.title: Linear versus exponential change
lessons.reading: A linear pattern adds a fixed amount, whereas an exponential pattern multiplies by a fixed factor. Compare differences and ratios in tables. A percentage change depends on the current amount, so equal percentages need not mean equal numerical changes.
lessons.worked: 100, 110, 120 is linear; 100, 110, 121 is exponential growth by 10%.

application.prompt: Which table follows exponential growth?
application.explanation: Each term is multiplied by 3. Constant multiplication distinguishes this from constant addition.

vocab.definition: The multiplier between consecutive terms of a geometric sequence.
The output at input zero in a model.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Each term is multiplied by 3. Constant multiplication distinguishes this from constant addition.

lessons.title: Interpret and compare models
lessons.reading: Interpret parameters, long-term trends, and realistic domains before calculating. A sequence of repeated percent changes is multiplicative. Percentage increases and decreases of the same size do not generally cancel because their starting amounts differ.
lessons.worked: Increasing 100 by 20% gives 120. Decreasing 120 by 20% gives 96.

application.prompt: After a 50% increase followed by a 50% decrease, $80 becomes…
application.explanation: 80 × 1.5 × 0.5 = 60. The decrease applies to the increased amount.

vocab.definition: A change divided by the original amount, expressed as a percentage.
A fixed value controlling a model's behavior.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: 80 × 1.5 × 0.5 = 60. The decrease applies to the increased amount.

lessons.title: Summarize one-variable data
lessons.reading: Use center and spread together. The median resists extreme values better than the mean. Standard deviation describes spread around the mean. Compare distributions using shape, center, spread, and unusual observations; a single statistic is not the whole story.
lessons.worked: For 2, 3, 4, 5, 100, the median is 4 while the mean is 22.8.

application.prompt: Which measure of center is usually less affected by one extreme high outlier?
application.explanation: An outlier can strongly move the sum and mean, but the median depends on ordered position.

vocab.definition: The middle value of ordered data.
A measure of typical spread around the mean.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: An outlier can strongly move the sum and mean, but the median depends on ordered position.

lessons.title: Association and residuals
lessons.reading: A scatter plot shows relationships between two quantitative variables. A residual is observed minus predicted output. Correlation describes linear association, not causation. Use context and residual patterns to judge whether a fitted model is reasonable.
lessons.worked: If a model predicts 12 but the observation is 15, the residual is 3.

application.prompt: Observed y is 9 and predicted y is 11. The residual is…
application.explanation: Residual = observed − predicted = 9 − 11 = −2.

vocab.definition: Observed output minus predicted output.
A measure of the direction and strength of linear association.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Residual = observed − predicted = 9 − 11 = −2.

lessons.title: Two-way tables and conclusions
lessons.reading: Two-way tables organize categorical data. Conditional relative frequencies use the relevant row or column total. A sample can be biased if selection favors a group. An observational association alone cannot establish that changing one variable causes another.
lessons.worked: If 12 of 20 bus riders arrive early, 60% of bus riders arrive early.

application.prompt: Of 30 students taking art, 18 also take music. What fraction of art students take music?
application.explanation: The condition is taking art, so the denominator is the 30 art students.

vocab.definition: A frequency calculated within a specified subgroup.
A systematic distortion caused by how a sample is selected.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: The condition is taking art, so the denominator is the 30 art students.
